items.title: Qwen Audio Agent + Claude Code: This Basically makes Claude Code a HUMAN!
items.summary:
In this video, I'll connect Qwen Audio Agent to Claude Code so I can keep a voice conversation going while the coding work runs in the background. First I'll explain how the voice front end, the local gateway and the Claude Code backend fit together, then install it with npm, set up the DashScope voice key, the Claude backend and the workspace, and start the gateway and the browser interface. Then I'll build a small issue tracker called VoiceDesk by voice, ask questions while it builds, interrupt the spoken answer, change a requirement mid-build and report a whitespace-title bug. Finally, I'll test cancelling a backend task, go over where this setup is useful and what it costs, and share the checks I'd judge it by.

--

🎙️ Qwen Audio Agent is an open-source app that connects a voice conversation to agents like Claude Code, with browser, terminal and desktop clients.

In this video, I'll show you CLI-Anything, an open-source project from HKUDS at the University of Hong Kong that gives any piece of software a command line interface your AI agent can use. I explain why a CLI with JSON output beats screenshot-based GUI automation, APIs and rewrites, and how it calls the real app instead of a toy copy. Then I show CLI-Hub, the package manager for ready-made CLIs, and the meta-skill that lets your agent find and install the right tool by itself. After that, I go through the CLI generator plugin in Claude Code and its seven phases, and we try the generated CLIs for GIMP, LibreOffice and Blender, plus the refine, test and validate commands. Finally, I cover HARNESS.md, the tests, the demos and the limitations.

items.title: Recursive Flint: This OPEN Local Coding Model is CRAZY! (Tested with Pi, OpenCode & PandaCode)
items.summary:
Join this channel to get access to perks:
https://www.youtube.com/channel/@aicodeking/join

In this video, I'll test Recursive Flint, a new open mixture-of-experts coding model with 40 billion parameters in total and only 2.5 billion active per token, built to run agentic coding on your own computer. I'll go over Recursive's claims, set it up on my M4 Max with llama.cpp after their own rec engine refused my Mac, and measure how fast it really is at short and long context. Then I'll show you how to use it in PandaCode with Pi and OpenCode, and put it through four real tasks: a landing page, a bug fix, a backend API and a Breakout game. I'm not testing it on KingBench, because it's a small local model and that wouldn't be fair, so I checked every result myself instead.

--
Key Takeaways:

🚀 Recursive Flint is an Apache 2.0 mixture-of-experts model with 40B total parameters and about 2.5B active per token, made for local agentic coding.
📊 Recursive claims it beats every MoE model under 50
